findings.text: the sentence states that the 54.6 ms against 1.27 ms contrast is a comparison across states, but both figures are at the diverted 550-cell state (the plan records 1.225 ms steady at that state) and the profiler arms compared were the unbatched rebuilding read (profile_kernels.py:117, no tracking so support_read.read takes the rebuild path) at 31.82 ms and the carried batched read at 31.61 ms, so the 1.27 ms carried unbatched read was never traced by this instrument; the paragraph also contradicts the one immediately above it, which attributes 49.57 ms of the same 54.61 ms to a per-call fixed cost at the same state.

the claim that the kernel count does not rise with the batch is read off a decrease (19,989 to 19,587) that is the signature of a top-12-by-time sum whose membership changed, and the log's own ADDED_KERNEL rows record 18 kernels scaling per slice (input_reduce_fusion_3 363 to 4,719 events), so the 1,473 difference is a delta between two differently-composed truncated sums rather than a launch count the batched path adds.
emit is a verbatim third copy of measure.py:42 and is imported nowhere, so the helper now has three definitions in one package and the file that owns it gains no caller.

the batch-1 loop_gather_fusion row is truncated by an interleaved TRACE_LINES write, so the log cannot be parsed as one JSON object per event line and the batch-1 figures the fragment quotes are recoverable only by subtracting the batch-4 sum from the combined total.
